decisive_items: ST segments elevated 4-6 mm in leads II, III and aVF, with ST depression in leads V2-V6
widespread ST-segment elevations (4-15 mm) in leads II, III, aVF, and V2-V6
10% stenosis in proximal left anterior descending artery (LAD) and right coronary artery (RCA)
response.rationale: The transient, alcohol-triggered ST elevations with near-normal coronary arteries are classic for coronary vasospasm (variant angina). The minimal stenosis supports vasospasm over fixed obstruction. Alcohol-induced arrhythmias (R2) could explain syncope and VT but not the diffuse ST elevations. Alcoholic cardiomyopathy (R3) and HCM (R4) lack the specific ECG pattern and normal coronaries.

rejected.why: No evidence of hypertrophy or obstructive physiology; ECG and angiography not consistent with HCM.
Chronic alcohol use is present, but the transient ST elevations and normal coronaries are not explained by alcoholic cardiomyopathy.
Arrhythmias are present, but the ST elevation pattern and alcohol-triggered episodes point to vasospasm rather than primary arrhythmia.
